subject: How to pull-out lod scores from a qtl model

messages.author: 09e9d545e0510a59
messages.subject: How to pull-out lod scores from a qtl model
parts:
Hi,

I am new to r/qtl. I am using an efficient published script (see attached) to generate QTLs for multiple traits in a tomato riself population. I want to generate a file with lod scores at every marker to be used in a genome browser (like IGV). In the first part of the script it is built-in the script with capture.output of the scanone item. The second part which is Model Selection and QTL refinement (uses makeqtl, addqtl, fitqtl, refineqtl and stepwiseqtl) doesn't really use a scan algorithm (like scantwo or mqmscan) but gave me good results. However, when I want to pull the lods scores to be used in a genome browser I couldn't find a way to do it. I was able to plot the refined QTLs using plotLodProfile, but couldn't pull out the lod scores.

Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks,

Itay

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to pull-out lod scores from a qtl model
parts:
The profile LOD scores from refineqtl() are stored as an attribute.

lodprof <- attr(qtlobject, "lodprofile")

This is a list of scanone objects

lodprof[[1]]
lodprof[[2]]

karl

Thank you so much for that Karl.

I got another question regarding that:

Is it possible to include the lod scores from the chromosomes that don't have a QTL in, so I would be able to create a single file with continuous positions across the genome with lod scores at each position. I guess I can pull these lods out from the scanone file and combine the two files not in r, but it would be much easier if I would be able to do it within r/qtl.

Thanks again

Itay

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to pull-out lod scores from a qtl model
parts:
Unfortunately, I don't have any easy way to do that at present.

The "simplest" thing would be to run addqtl() to get a scanone object with the results for all of the other chromosomes, and then plug in the profileLOD results (provided that there are no linked QTL, in which case there would be overlapping sets of LOD scores).

sorry,
karl
